## Lead to owner: inbound lead routing for HubSpot
A new form lead gets an owner (or the right queue) within minutes, with the reason written on the record: duplicates checked, the AI reads the message, Clay fills missing fields, a fit and engagement score, nine ordered rules, a Slack message for the new owner.

All logic is in the Code nodes, built from the tested files in `src/` (`npm test`, `npm run build`). Settings live in `src/config.js`. Every name, ID and number in this sample is made up.

Before you publish or activate it: pick the five credentials, set the Clay webhook URL, create the `lr_` properties in HubSpot (README).

### 1. Intake and duplicates
Skip repeats, and leads that already have an owner or were already routed. Exact email-key duplicates merge at the end; a company found by name only can decide the owner but is not linked.

### 2. AI before Clay
Claude labels intent from the form text only (no name or email). Support, job seekers and spam never spend Clay credits. Clay gets 2 minutes.

### 3. Score and route
Nine rules, first match wins. The round robin reads HubSpot, so there is no counter to keep in sync.

### 4. Write back and tell people
Update first, merge last. Slack replies are checked.

### Watchdog
Every 5 minutes: leads that entered the workflow, were never routed and have no owner (a failed run, an API outage). Each one is reported once.

### Monday numbers
Time to owner, share inside 5 minutes, misses, review flags and key-field fill rate, posted to #sales-routing.
